title: Operator Simulation Syllabus and Skill Validation Catalog
author: Sofia Patel
content:
Summary

This page defines a repeatable syllabus for platform operator simulations, a catalog of hands‑on labs, and a structured skill validation rubric. The goal is to make oncall readiness measurable and repeatable across teams that operate Redwood’s inference platform. This document is intended for platform operators, platform SREs, and engineers who run or observe incident simulations.

Goals

- Provide a modular curriculum for running platform incident simulations (gamedays) with measurable learning outcomes.
- Teach observable runbook execution, triage discipline, and safe mitigation patterns for LLM inference services.
- Produce a canonical set of lab exercises operators can run locally or in the sandbox fleet.
- Provide an assessment rubric and a retro template so teams can measure improvement over time.

Audience

- Platform operators, site reliability engineers, platform QA, and junior engineers preparing for oncall rotations.

Prerequisites

- Familiarity with platform observability (Prometheus/Tempo/Tracing, internal dashboards).
- Access to the operator sandbox namespace (ask Platform Lab: self‑serve access).
- Basic familiarity with CLI tools: redwoodctl, kubectl, and the internal operator UI.

Curriculum Overview (Modules)

1) Fundamentals: Observability & Mental Models (1 session, 2 hours)
   - Learning objectives: read SLO dashboards, interpret per‑tenant token cost graphs, and map alerts to potential root causes.
   - Topics: SLI taxonomy, token‑cost attribution, KV cache heatmaps, request path call graphs.

2) Controlled Degradation: Prefetch / KV Cache Failure (2 sessions, 3 hours)
   - Learning objectives: identify cache miss storms, run the cache‑drain runbook, and test graceful prefetch fallback.
   - Lab: simulate KV cache shard offline, force synthetic prefix churn, verify fallback to warmset and measure tail latency.

3) Capacity Scarcity: Tenant Eviction and Fairness (2 sessions, 3 hours)
   - Learning objectives: apply eviction thresholds, reconcile tenant credits, and run emergency buydown.
   - Lab: trigger a tenant burst, use the eviction simulator to claim capacity, and execute soft‑eviction.

4) Model Variant Fallback and Quality Regression (2 sessions, 3 hours)
   - Learning objectives: switch model variant rollout safely, validate regression tests, confirm fallback policy works under overload.
   - Lab: flip traffic using canary DSL, validate evaluation prompts, and observe degradation alerts.

5) Multi‑Region Failover and Routing (2 sessions, 3 hours)
   - Learning objectives: verify regional routing policies, practice cross‑region failover, and observe cache warmup costs.
   - Lab: simulate regional partition and run operator‑guided failover.

6) Post‑incident Communication & Retro (1 session, 90 minutes)
   - Learning objectives: run a concise retro using the Incident Hypothesis Canvas, assign remediation actions, and update runbooks/dashboards.

Lab Catalog (practical exercises you can run in the sandbox)

Each lab includes: objective, setup commands, verification checks, rollback.

A) KV Cache Shard Failover (sandbox)
- Objective: validate graceful KV shard handoff and prefix cache rehydration.
- Setup:
  1. Mark node: redwoodctl node taint cache-shard-3 NoSchedule --reason=simulate-failure
  2. Trigger eviction: redwoodctl simulate cache-shard-failure --shard=3 --duration=600s
- Verification:
  - Dashboard: prefix_cache_miss_rate (should spike then converge)
  - Check: curl -sS 'https://sandbox-op/health/prefix-cache' | jq .status
- Rollback:
  - redwoodctl node untaint cache-shard-3
  - Confirm prefix cache steady state in 2–5 minutes

B) Emergency Model Swap (canary then rollback)
- Objective: run a safe model swap when a larger model is causing token cost regressions.
- Setup:
  1. Open canary: redwoodctl canary start --route=model-gen --variant=smaller-quantized:v2
  2. Apply traffic weight: redwoodctl canary set-weight --id=1234 --percent=10
- Verification:
  - Latency SLO: p95 < 1600ms for canary traffic
  - Quality: run 20 eval prompts: redwood-eval run --canary 1234 --suite=smoke-qa
- Rollback:
  - redwoodctl canary abort --id=1234

C) Tenant Burst Eviction Play (operator simulator)
- Objective: practice decision canvas for fair share and tenant buydown.
- Steps:
  1. Launch synthetic load: redwoodctl loadgen start --tenant=synthetic-burster --rps=1200 --tokens=10k
  2. Monitor: tenant_token_consumption_total by tenant
  3. Run eviction: redwoodctl tenant eviction --tenant=synthetic-burster --policy=soft
- Verification: eviction reduces q-length and token burn within 90s

Assessment Rubric (skills to validate during or after a simulation)

- Triage speed: 0–15m (A), 15–30m (B), 30–60m (C), >60m (D)
- Correct diagnosis: root cause identified (yes/no)
- Runbook fidelity: followed documented steps (yes/partial/no)
- Safe mitigation: used non‑destructive fallback first (yes/partial/no)
- Communication: clear status updates every 10–15 minutes (yes/partial/no)
- Postmortem: action items created with owners and due dates (yes/no)

Scoring guidance: A = majority A grades and yes for critical items; simulation certification requires A or B overall.

Runbook & Dashboard Mapping

Use this quick mapping to pick which runbook and dashboards to include in a sim: 

| Scenario | Primary runbook | Dashboards to show | Minimum alert set | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| KV cache failure | cache-drain-and-rebuild-runbook | prefix_cache_miss_rate, cache_rehydration_time, tail_latency | cache_miss_spike > 5x | Cache team |
| Tenant burst | tenant-eviction-and-soft-buydown | tenant_token_consumption_total, queue_length_by_tenant | tenant_token_rate > threshold | Capacity team |
| Model variant regression | model-variant-fallback-runbook | per_variant_latency, eval-passrate | eval_regression_alert | ML infra |
| Regional partition | regional-failover-runbook | cross_region_p95, interregion_rtt | region_health_down | Network infra |

Alerting playbook (during a simulation)

1) Acknowledge alerts and set incident channel: /incident create "Sim: <scenario>" --visibility=private
2) Assign roles: Incident Lead, Triage, Mitigation, Communications.
3) Run triage checklist (5 items):
   a) Confirm symptoms on dashboards
   b) Confirm affected tenants/services
   c) Check for correlated deployments or infra changes
   d) Identify immediate mitigations (fallbacks/evictions/circuit-breakers)
   e) Execute non‑destructive mitigation first
4) Track timeline in the incident channel and log operator commands used.

Retro template (one page summary to paste into postmortem)

- Title: [Sim] <scenario> — <date>
- Participants: 
- Timeline (bullet list with timestamps)
- What went well (3 bullets)
- What to improve (3 bullets)
- Action items (table):
  - Action | Owner | Due date | Status
  - e.g. "Add dashboard to show per‑canary eval passrate" | Marco Li | 2026-02-01 | open

Sandbox safety rules

- Simulations must use the sandbox or designated synthetic tenants. Do not run destructive operations against production.
- If a safe window in canary overlaps production routes, reduce traffic weights to <= 5% and notify the SRE rotation lead.
- All simulations must be scheduled on the platform lab calendar and have an observer from the platform ops team.

Implementation roadmap (next 12 months)

- Q2 2026: Add automated scoring harness that parses incident channel logs and assigns rubric grades (MVP).
- Q3 2026: Expand lab catalog with thermal/spot instance simulations.
- Q4 2026: Integrate skill validation into new‑hire platform onboarding and certify 90% of new oncall engineers.
- Q1 2027: Publish an anonymized simulation results dashboard for leadership and training insights.

Ownership and maintenance

- Document owner: Platform Training (team alias: platform-lab@redwood.com)
- Quarterly review cadence: Platform Training + Eng Platform (quarterly)
- Update policy: update module content after each public simulation with actionable retro items.

Related resources

- Operator runbook writing guide: /confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/runbook-authoring-and-maintenance-guidelines-2025
- Simulation automation playbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/platform-gameday-exercise-automation-and-scripting-playbook-2026
- Incident Hypothesis Canvas template: /confluence/templates/incident-hypothesis-canvas

Appendix: Quick CLI cheatsheet

- Open sandbox node taint: redwoodctl node taint <node> NoSchedule --reason="simulate-failure"
- Start canary: redwoodctl canary start --route=<route> --variant=<variant>
- Start loadgen: redwoodctl loadgen start --tenant=<id> --rps=<n>

If you have questions or want to run a bespoke simulation for your team, ping platform-lab@redwood.com and include a brief objective and preferred week.
